newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Army commandoes free kidnapped officials.
newsitem.headline: Army commandoes free kidnapped officials.

text.p: Bangladesh army commandos on Tuesday freed six government officials abducted last month by tribal insurgents in the southern Chittagong Hills Tracts, security officials said.
The commandos, acting on a tipoff, launched a dawn raid on a jungle rebel hide-out in Thanch, bordering the Indian state of Mizoram, freeing the officials and two other civilians, they said.
The Shanti Bahini (Peace Force) rebels fled across the border leaving behind arms and ammunition.
The officials were flown by military helicopter to Bandarban town, 100 km (60 miles) from Chittagong port.
The officials were abducted on November 29 from Baganchara valley in Bandarban. The rebels were demanding an undisclosed ransom.

Tribal insurgents have been fighting a bush war for autonomy of 5,500 sq miles (14,200 sq km) of hill tracts bordering India and Burma. They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency since it began in 1973.
